Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Construction, trades & building materials

addition noun

something added

also an addition, a new addition, extension, add-on

classical

Cic. Off. 1.138: accessiōnem adjūnxit aedibus
Cic. Lael. 11: paucōrum annōrum accessiō

accessiō, accessiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an addition; something added on, an extension

From accēdere, to come to, be added: what is added is said to accēdere, as in accēdit quod, there is also the fact that (see further). Lewis & Short: “the thing added, the addition”.

Examples

  • Hanc Scaurus dēmōlītus accessiōnem adjūnxit aedibus.

    Scaurus pulled it down and added it to his own house as an extension.Cic. Off. 1.138

  • Quid igitur hunc paucōrum annōrum accessiō juvāre potuisset?

    So what good could the addition of a few years have done him?Cic. Lael. 11

Other words

  • additāmentum, additāmentī n. — an addition, something tacked on

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 68: Ligus iste nescio quī, additāmentum inimīcōrum meōrum; Sen. Ep. 17.6 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare: once in Cicero, of a nobody who merely swells the ranks of his enemies; then Seneca (Lewis & Short).

  • adjectiō, adjectiōnis f. — the adding of something, an addition

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.30.6: Rōmānam rem nūper etiam adjectiōne populī Albānī auctam

See also further, add, increase.

SourcesLewis & Short: accessio · Lewis & Short: additamentum · Lewis & Short: adjectio
